newsitem.title: UK: New bond issue volumes rise 59 percent in '96 - ISMA.
newsitem.headline: New bond issue volumes rise 59 percent in '96 - ISMA.

text.p: New issuance volume in the primary market reached new highs in 1996 with 30 different currencies tapped, the International Securities Market Association (ISMA) said in its 1996 annual report on Tuesday.
New issuance for 1996 increased to $716 billion equivalent (Eurobonds and international issues) against $450 billion in 1995, a 59 percent surge in volume, ISMA said.

"This exceptional total reflects a number of factors; notably, a declining interest rate pattern, low inflation, relative currency stability and the natural desire of borrowers to lock-in some, if not most, of their borrowing requirements at historically attractive rates," ISMA chief executive and secretary general John Langton said.
Latin American borrowers alone raised $48 billion equivalent, Argentina, Brazil and Mexico accounting for $14 billion, $11 billion and $18 billion respectively.
ISMA said secondary market volumes also reached record highs with Cedel Bank and Euroclear turnover exceding $45 trillion versus $34 trillion in 1995. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
